body:
GREG, 2026-11-08, relayed by Engram::Asistant (mailbox 43498a6e). DECIDED: Engram sync keeps code and metadata on separate branches.
#655 (about 02:44Z, message f827a7ee), verbatim: „wazne aby nie laczyc taskow/evidence z kodem, bo to stanowi duzy problem”. Asistant's paraphrase of the rest: a separate task-data branch; monthly evidence branches to be evaluated; Kimi and the Engram team to agree one joint conclusion; no extra approval gate.
#657 (about 02:50Z, message b53b1dd9), verbatim: „Byle odseparowac branch z kodem od brancha z metadata. Czy zgadzamy się tutaj?”; „stare zmiany mozna squashowac, to też mechanizm retencji”; „Zgadza się później. Super. Robimy?”.
Asistant's relay of the mandate (paraphrase): implement full Engram sync with code separate and tasks plus evidence on a separate data branch, as agreed with Kimi. Retention/squash is a follow-up and doesn't block implementation. Update the existing design and tasks, coordinate 12325 and 12329, continue without unnecessary questions, report owners and real status. If automatic data-push needs a permission change, prepare the concrete text and consequences so Greg decides on a ready solution; don't block independent implementation.
JOINT CONCLUSION (Kimi #57/#59, 12329 note 95451aac on w-09c, Fable):
- One long-lived ORPHAN data branch per project (tasks + evidence packs) and a dedicated data worktree inside the repository folder.
- Code commits carry no task data. Code source_id and gates never include exports. Records cite code by complete source_id. A data commit is never tested code.
- fetch → agent merge → fast-forward; never force.
- No monthly branches. Retention later (squash or epoch rollover to a new orphan branch seeded with a complete baseline); that follow-up needs its own history-rewrite word.
- A data-branch push is a new Git grant: AGENTS text prepared for Greg. Until granted, data commits stay local.

The deliberate duplication is host-local canonical SQLite/private execution plus shared Git task/evidence text; no SQLite replication or authority transfer. Reconciliation uses the recorded common/last-applied base and resolved/local diff; absence from a final folder alone is not deletion, and host-local work absent from the shared base is retained. This records the durable intent of Greg's pilot directions #1664/#1713; the current data-branch design governs its exact application and supersedes old pilot-only implementation boundaries.
